title: Prove the relay-hub normal form of the P104 native word, a descent-crossing bound and a pair-exchange frame law (no κ)
body:
**No new κ.** Four exact statements about legal native words, replayed on the literal #6824 native word.

**Hub normal form.** Events at the zero frame on registers that start at `{0}` (`K`) commute to the start and events at the full frame on registers that end full (`R`) commute to the end. With `T` the invertible map of the rest and `A = I + E`, gauges `G0` on `K`, `G9` on `R` with `G9·T·G0 = A` exist iff `T[R̄,K̄] = A[R̄,K̄]`, `T[R,Hnn] = 0`, `T[Hnn,K] = 0` and `rank T[R,K] = |H09|` (equivalently `≤`). The first condition with its dual `T⁻¹[K̄,R̄] = A⁻¹[K̄,R̄]` is not sufficient when `Hnn ≠ ∅` (two-register control). There is no dyadic obstruction: a gauge over `Z[1/2]` exists iff those conditions hold and `T ∈ GL(Z[1/2])`, with an explicit completion. Feed-forward corollary: if all helpers start at `{0}` and end full, the mid map never writes `X` or reads `Y` and `T[Y,X] = E`, a dyadic gauge exists whenever `T[H,H] ∈ GL(Z[1/2])`. On the #6824 word (|K| = 556, |R| = 571, |H09| = 359, |Hnn| = 4) all conditions hold exactly, `rank T[R,K] = 359`, `T⁻¹` is dyadic (denominators up to 64), and the gauge re-solved from `T` alone gives a legal word with identical MOVE events and the exact endpoint on all 772 rows (37,819 events against 18,622; 14 never-moving private lifetimes removed).

**Descent-crossing bound.** For an up-set `U` of frames, at least `rank A[final ∉ U, init ∈ U]` private descents lead from `U` to outside `U`. For pairwise odd ports this is the clique size: the clique number is 8 and each of the 759 maximum cliques is crossed by exactly 8 of the 24 descents (the bound is attained).

**Scheduling.** Every linear extension of the per-register event order is legal with the same endpoint, frame chains and invoice histograms; only the number of simultaneously live private registers changes (14 to 29 over ten random schedules; the word has 14). Scheduling alone cannot change the price of a fixed network.

**Pair-exchange law.** If the outputs of an exchange at frame `G` reach sinks `s1`, `s2` along paths without a private descent, then `G ⊆ final(s1) ∩ final(s2)`; two distinct 8-dimensional sink frames force `dim G ≤ 7`. Registers 679 and 686 exchange at a frame of dimension 7 that equals the intersection of the sink frames 175 and 226. Without the descent hypothesis the inclusion fails (1,559 events); all 645,102 (event, sink) pairs reached without descents satisfy it.

**Overlap.** The wall, the 5824 odd pairs and the E8 structure are #6831 section 6 (cited, not repeated); the up-set bound extends its argument. Ali Romman's dyadic helper-basis completion and #6827 concern bases at interior cuts, not zero-frame and full-frame events; #6345 shows that the price depends on the rank histograms only. Repository text search found no other statement of these items (prose may be missed).

**Not established.** The rewritten word is a witness of the freedom, has more events than the original (it exceeds the 26,000-event bound of the default profile; the package declares no event bound) and is not re-priced; the native chart checks and the five framework assumptions of #6824 are not re-run (its MOVE events and chart pairs are identical). The unit-pivot completion is a greedy rule that succeeded here; general existence is the theorem. The pair-exchange law gives no cost for alternatives. All arithmetic is exact rational (no modular rank or inverse).

Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a. The one executable input is the #6824 native word (head 2a7ca44fbda3abaa4df355b183ed7d7478eef7c1), rebuilt by that pull request's own construction and pinned by Git blob, SHA-256 and its published payload digest `d3ccfce7bdbca3b79771844e6c9fee48f1a8066444a19218995648df96982821` in `retained/SOURCE-PINS.json`.

Reproduce (CPython 3.12, standard library, about 15 s per run):
```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-relay-hub-normal-form
```
Expected: `PASS_RELAY_HUB_NORMAL_FORM` (normal and `-O`) and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.
